The fire is the kitchen

At Kiln there is no backstage. You sit at a stainless-steel counter and the chefs cook your food over charcoal, an arm's length away — smoke, heat and all.

Kiln is Ben Chapman's live-fire restaurant on Brewer Street — Northern Thai cooking built around the grill: skewers kissed by coals, clay pots baked in the heat, whole flavours of smoke in everything.

It is part of Super 8 Restaurants, the group behind Smoking Goat, Brat and Mountain — and it holds a MICHELIN Bib Gourmand and a place on World's 50 Best Discovery.

Two ways in

The counter upstairs runs on nerve and timing — first come, first seated. The room downstairs runs on a booking. Pick your way in.

Upstairs · Walk-in only

The Counter

Stoop at the stainless-steel counter, watch your dinner cross the coals, eat it the second it lands. No bookings up here — join the queue on Brewer Street.

Downstairs · Bookable

The Downstairs Room

The one part of Kiln you can plan around: the downstairs dining room takes bookings for parties of four or more. Same fire, your own table, a date in the diary.
